Below the research vessel, a remotely operated submersible descended through dark blue water. Its lamps revealed a steep wall of rock covered with pale corals. The pilot slowed the thrusters near a narrow crevice and guided a sampling arm toward loose sediment. Tiny particles drifted upward when the container closed.

A marine biologist reviewed the camera feed from the control room. She noted a cluster of translucent animals beside a thermal plume, then compared the recorded depth with a chart of nearby currents. The team labeled the specimen tray and scheduled another dive after sunrise.

On the deck, technicians inspected the cable drum and listened for irregular motion in the winch. Salt spray had coated the connectors, so each contact was cleaned and sealed. The vessel held its position as the last instrument rose from the sea.
